h1: Pineapple Guesthouse — a warm, family-run budget stay a 5-minute walk from Karon Beach
intro: If you want to stay right by Karon Beach for the price of a few hundred baht, in a clean air-conditioned room run by hosts who treat you like family, Pineapple Guesthouse is a name budget travelers have passed around for years · It's a small guesthouse on Patak Road, run by the same family for over 20 years · about a 5-minute walk to Karon Beach, with a little café out front serving breakfast and coffee · Rooms range from Standard up to a Family Room, and all have air-conditioning, a TV, a large fridge and hot water · From approx. ฿700/night (higher in high season) · scored 9.0 from over 500 reviews on Booking.com.

body.html: What sets Pineapple Guesthouse apart from the usual budget options in Phuket is that it's a genuine family guesthouse · It has been opened and run by the same family for more than 20 years, and countless reviews mention owners and a manager who remember your face, call you a taxi, and recommend restaurants and boat trips as if you were a relative dropping by · The building is a multi-storey shophouse on Patak Road in the Karon Beach area, about a 5-minute walk from the sand · Understand up front that this is not a hotel or resort with a grand lobby and a pool — it's a simple, clean place to sleep at a price you can actually afford, which is exactly why people come back and tell their friends.

There are around six room types, starting with Standard King and Standard Twin rooms (roughly 18–22 sqm), the plainest and cheapest option · Above those sit Balcony King and Balcony Twin rooms with a private balcony to sit out on · a Triple Room for three · up to the Family Room, a larger two-king-bed room with a separate bathroom, a microwave and a Smart TV, made for families · Reviews consistently praise that every room has air-conditioning, a cable TV, a large fridge, a safe and hot water · Many guests say the rooms are cleaner and more spacious than they expected at this price · Worth knowing: bathrooms are wet-room style (the shower shares the space with the toilet), typical of a guesthouse, and some of the cheapest rooms have few windows or little natural light — if that matters to you, choose a room with a balcony or a window.

"The room was clean, the bed comfortable, the A/C cold, and it's only a few minutes' walk to Karon Beach · But what stayed with me were the owners — so kind, arranging our transport and pointing us to the good spots. It felt like staying at a friend's house, and far better value than what we paid."

Another part of its charm is the small café out front · In the morning it serves a homemade breakfast, fresh coffee and simple dishes like eggs and toast, along with curries and Thai food that reviewers say are tasty and well priced · Note that breakfast is usually pay-as-you-go rather than bundled into every room rate, so check when you book · Beyond the café, the front desk handles a tour desk, airport transfers, luggage storage and a safe · Service is the highest-rated category here (around 9.1 on Agoda), which says a lot: the heart of Pineapple isn't the plushness of the rooms, it's the people who run it.

The location is another reason it's such good value · The guesthouse sits on Patak Road in Karon, about a 5-minute walk from the beach — Karon is a long, wide white-sand beach that's noticeably calmer than Patong, ideal if you want a quieter shore · Around the guesthouse you'll find restaurants, massage shops, convenience stores, banks and the Karon Temple Market, all within walking distance · Kata Beach is about 10 minutes by car, the Karon–Kata Viewpoint about 15 minutes, Patong roughly 25–30 minutes, and Phuket Airport about 50–60 minutes · That means you can walk to the beach and out to eat by day without relying on a car, and only need a Grab or a scooter when you head to other beaches or the old town.

There are several honest caveats, because this is a budget guesthouse, not a hotel · First — there's no on-site pool; guests who want to swim can walk up the hill and use a nearby hotel's pool for a daily fee, but if a pool is a must-have, this isn't the place · Second — the building is multi-storey with no elevator, so you'll climb stairs; anyone with heavy luggage or who struggles with steps should ask for a ground-floor room when booking · Third — bathrooms are wet-room style and some of the cheaper rooms are plain and a little dated, with limited natural light · Fourth — because it's on a street in a tourist area, some nights carry a little traffic or noise from nearby shops · The rooms category scores around 8.1, the lowest of all — that reflects these points, while value (8.9) and service (9.1) are what pull the overall score up high.

So who is Pineapple Guesthouse for? · Most clearly, budget travelers, couples, solo travelers and backpackers who want a clean, private, air-conditioned room right by Karon Beach, leaving plenty of budget for exploring and eating · It suits people who value the location and the owners' care more than the polish of the room · Those who should look elsewhere are travelers who want a beachfront resort with a pool and hotel-style facilities (see KK - Karon Kata or Baan Karonburi in this same list), anyone who can't manage stairs, and those expecting a spotless, modern room throughout · Set your expectations to "budget guesthouse" and it delivers value that's hard to find in Karon.

A few tips from reading through the real reviews here: ask for a ground-floor room if you're carrying heavy bags, and choose a room with a balcony or window for natural light, since some of the cheaper rooms are on the dark side · Ask about breakfast and using the neighbouring hotel's pool at check-in · Walk down to Karon Beach in the late afternoon for the sunset — Karon faces west and the light is lovely · And use the guesthouse's tour desk and airport transfer, or have them arrange a scooter rental, since public transport around Karon and Kata is sparse.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Pineapple Guesthouse Phuket

faq.q: Where is Pineapple Guesthouse in Phuket, and can you walk to the beach?
faq.a: It's at 291/4 Patak Road in the Karon Beach area, Mueang Phuket district · about a 5-minute walk to Karon Beach, a wide white-sand beach that's calmer than Patong · Restaurants, massage shops, convenience stores, banks and the Karon Temple Market are all within walking distance · Kata Beach is about 10 minutes by car and Phuket Airport about 50–60 minutes.

faq.q: How much does Pineapple Guesthouse cost, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around ฿700/night for a Standard room · There are about six room types, from Standard King/Twin, Balcony King/Twin (with a balcony) and a Triple Room up to a Family Room with two king beds, a separate bathroom and a microwave · Prices rise in high season, so compare a few platforms and check the total before booking.

faq.q: Does Pineapple Guesthouse have a pool and breakfast?
faq.a: There's no on-site swimming pool, but you can walk to a nearby hotel's pool and use it for a daily fee · For breakfast there's a café out front serving breakfast, coffee and affordable Thai food, though it's usually pay-as-you-go rather than included in every room rate — check when you book.

faq.q: Who is Pineapple Guesthouse best for?
faq.a: It's great for budget travelers, couples, solo travelers and backpackers who want a clean, private, air-conditioned room right by Karon Beach at an affordable price · It suits people who value the location and the owners' care over luxury · It's less suited to travelers who want a beachfront resort with a pool or full hotel facilities.

faq.q: What should I know before booking Pineapple Guesthouse?
faq.a: As a budget guesthouse, the building is multi-storey with no elevator, so ask for a ground-floor room if you carry heavy bags · Bathrooms are wet-room style and some cheaper rooms are plain or dark, so choose a room with a balcony or window and view photos of each type before booking · Being on a street in a tourist area, some nights carry a little noise.

faq.q: Is it convenient to stay here without a car?
faq.a: For short distances, yes — you can walk to the beach, restaurants and the market · But to reach other beaches, the old town or Patong, public transport around Karon and Kata is sparse, so use Grab or rent a scooter · The guesthouse offers airport transfers and a tour desk and can arrange these in advance.
